name: Travel Cost Estimator
description: Price a business trip from live fares in your corporate booking tool, benchmark the non-bookable lines against your own approved expense reports, and produce an estimate a manager can approve — with a hard guardrail that never enters the booking funnel.
author: Al Macey
coverImageAlt: Travel components and expense evidence feed a balanced estimate folio while an orange gate blocks the booking path.
coverImagePrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: AI.Tedt.org skill gallery cover
Primary request: Create a premium editorial illustration that communicates assembling a manager-ready business travel estimate from live fare signals and approved expense evidence while stopping safely before booking.
Scene/backdrop: A warm paper-toned planning table with a miniature travel landscape: an abstract aircraft form, a hotel block, ground transport, meal tokens, and archived expense slips arranged as evidence rather than a consumer travel advertisement.
Subject: Multiple travel-cost components flow through a precise balancing scale into one clean estimate folio, while a distinct orange safety gate blocks the route before a distant departure portal, making estimate-only intent unmistakable without words.
Style/medium: Premium editorial illustration with tactile dimensional detail, layered cut paper, matte ceramic travel objects, brushed metal scale, translucent acrylic data paths, restrained enterprise craftsmanship.
Composition/framing: Exact 16:10 landscape; evidence sources on the left, balanced estimate at center, guarded boundary on the right; central scale and folio dominate; generous warm negative space; crop-safe focal subject; no essential detail in the outer 8%.
Lighting/mood: Calm, capable, quietly technical; measured studio lighting, trustworthy financial clarity, cautious forward planning.
Color palette: Warm paper #F8F6F0, slate #101820, navy #00446F, cyan #00A9E0, sparing orange #E86027.
Constraints: No text, letters, numbers, currency symbols, logos, trademarks, or watermark; no paw imagery or paw logo; no cats or cat silhouettes; no product UI or Microsoft Fluent branding. No boarding passes, readable receipts, branded aircraft, credit cards, booking confirmation, or travel-site interface.
